headline: Supreme Court Collegium Clarifies That New Chief Justice Appointments Will Now Require A Performance-Based 'Coolness Rating' From Local Court Canteen Staff
body: The Supreme Court has issued a directive requiring all prospective High Court Chief Justices to undergo a mandatory taste-test evaluation by senior canteen staff, ensuring the new appointees are capable of appreciating the structural integrity of a proper samosa. The final judicial seal will only be granted once the nominee receives a minimum 'extra-chatni' rating from the canteen’s longest-serving tea-bearer.
caption: Justice is served, usually alongside a cutting chai and a slightly soggy kachori. Do you trust your local court’s canteen staff to pick the next boss? #Judiciary #CanteenCulture #IndiaNews #Law (satire)
igHook: Would you trust your local court's tea-bearer to choose the next Chief Justice?
imagePrompt: A candid, medium-shot photo of a dimly lit, crowded courthouse canteen with wooden benches, featuring a stack of stainless steel plates in the foreground and blurred figures in lawyer robes chatting in the background.

sourceHeadline.title: SC Collegium Recommends Appointment Of Chief Justices At 4 High Courts

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 3 wins by grounding the absurdity in a specific, culturally resonant detail (the canteen samosa/extra-chatni rating) that feels like a genuine, affectionate observation of Indian bureaucracy. It avoids the 'formulaic' trap better than the others and provides a clear, vivid image of the courtroom culture.
